setup.teamsRequirements: This setup requires a Microsoft 365 work or school organization where you can register an Entra app, create an Azure Bot, and upload or install a Teams app. Personal or free Teams accounts at teams.live.com cannot complete this setup. This release supports Microsoft 365 commercial cloud tenants only; GCC, GCC High, DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet are not supported yet.
setup.teamsStep1: In Microsoft Entra, create a single-tenant app registration. Copy its Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID, then create a client secret and copy its value.
setup.teamsStep2: In Azure, create an Azure Bot. Choose Single Tenant, use that Application ID, set its messaging endpoint to the Paperclip URL below, and add the Microsoft Teams channel.
setup.teamsStep3: In Teams Developer Portal, create an app, add a bot with the same Application ID, then apply the manifest settings shown below. The block binds the Teams resource-specific consent permissions to that Entra app; these are not Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra. These permissions let the installed app receive every message in a team or group chat without an @mention, so describe that access to installers. Download the package and install it in the target team or group chat.
setup.fieldMapIntro: Use these exact portal sections and reuse the same Application ID in all three places.
setup.fieldMap1: {{entra}}: select {{newRegistration}}, choose {{accounts}}, then select {{register}}. Copy {{appClientId}} and {{tenantId}}. Under {{certificates}}, select {{newClientSecret}} and copy its {{value}}, not its Secret ID.
setup.fieldMap2: {{azure}}: set {{microsoftAppId}} to {{singleTenant}}, set {{creationType}} to {{useExisting}}, and enter the Application ID and Tenant ID above. After creation, open {{configuration}} and paste the Paperclip {{messagingEndpoint}}; then open {{channels}} and enable {{microsoftTeams}}.
setup.fieldMap3: {{apps}}: select {{newApp}}. Under {{configure}}, add an existing bot using the same Application ID; enable {{personal}}, {{team}}, and {{groupChat}} scopes plus file support. Under {{permissions}}, add the two RSC {{application}} permissions shown below. Complete the required app details and icons, explain that the app can receive every message in an installed team or group chat, then download the app package.
setup.fieldMap4: {{manageApps}}: select {{uploadApp}}, choose the downloaded package, and install it in each intended personal chat, group chat, or team. One team install covers its standard channels. Private and shared channels require a separate app installation and are not supported by this release. If upload is unavailable, a Teams administrator must enable or approve custom apps.
setup.manifestHint: Enter the Application / Client ID above before copying so the block contains the real bot identity. This block contains the Paperclip-specific fields to verify in Developer Portal or merge into a complete Teams app manifest. It is not a complete app package; Developer Portal supplies the remaining required metadata and packages the manifest with your app icons.
setup.ssoNote: Paperclip does not use Teams single sign-on in this release. The copied webApplicationInfo entry only associates the RSC permissions with the same Entra Application ID. Its nonempty resource is an RSC placeholder; you do not need to register an Entra Application ID URI or add delegated Microsoft Graph permissions.
setup.rscNote: The two application RSC permissions let the bot receive every message, without an @mention, in each team or group chat where it is installed. Paperclip retains and acts only on messages admitted by your Paperclip reach and access rules. Make this provider access clear in the app description shown to installers.
setup.channelsNote: This release supports personal chats, group chats, and standard team channels—not private channels. supportsFiles: true enables native file receipt and consent-based sending in personal chats; channel and group-chat files need a separate Microsoft Graph connection and are not ingested here.
setup.teamsHttpsWarning: Configure a public HTTPS URL for this Paperclip instance before connecting Microsoft Teams.

setup.githubStep1: Under the target user or organization, create a new GitHub App. Give it a globally unique name (34 characters or fewer), use the Paperclip homepage URL below, and leave user authorization off.
setup.githubStep2: Keep {{webhooksActive}} on. Enter the Paperclip webhook URL and the Paperclip-generated webhook secret below, and keep {{sslVerification}} selected.
setup.githubStep3: Under Repository permissions, set {{issues}} and {{pullRequests}} to {{readWrite}}. Leave every other permission at its default; Metadata remains read-only.
setup.githubStep4: Subscribe to {{issueComment}} ({{issueCommentCode}}), {{prReviewComment}} ({{prReviewCode}}). GitHub sends installation and installation_repositories to every GitHub App automatically; they are not selectable here.
setup.githubStep5: Choose {{onlyThisAccount}}, create the App, copy its App ID, generate one private key, then install it on the selected repositories.

slack.reconnect: Reconnect verifies or replaces credentials for this same Slack app. It does not reinstall the app or change its workspace or channel membership.
slack.remove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved Slack credentials. It does not uninstall the Slack app: the app remains installed, and its bot remains in channels, until you remove them in Slack.

github.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same App and installation, then updates its webhook URL, secret, and secure delivery settings. It does not reinstall the App or change repository access.
github.remove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved App key and webhook secret. It does not uninstall the GitHub App: the App, its installations, and its webhook settings remain until you remove or update them on GitHub.

discord.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Discord application and server installation. It does not add or remove the bot from the server.
discord.remove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops its Paperclip Gateway connection, and retires its saved bot token. It does not uninstall the bot: the bot remains in the Discord server, and the application remains in the Developer Portal, until you remove them there.

teams.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Microsoft app, tenant, and bot identity. It does not upload or reinstall the Teams app.
teams.remove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved client secret. It does not uninstall the Teams app: the Entra app registration, Azure Bot, custom Teams app, and Teams installations remain until you remove them in Microsoft.

photon.reconnect: Reconnect verifies the same Photon project and line allocation, then recovers eligible missed messages.
photon.remove: Disconnect archives this channel and removes its saved secret. Your Photon project, number, subscription, and Messages history remain in Photon.

telegram.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same BotFather bot and automatically refreshes its Paperclip webhook and command menu.
telegram.remove: Paperclip archives the endpoint and queues durable removal of its Telegram webhook and command menu. After Telegram confirms that cleanup, Paperclip retires the saved token. The BotFather bot and its chat memberships remain until you remove them in Telegram.

resolution.uploadUnknown: The file may already exist in OneDrive. Cancelling stops this Paperclip transfer; it does not delete remote bytes. Uploads cannot be marked delivered or retried from this uncertain state.
resolution.sendLost: Paperclip lost confirmation after sending. Check the provider conversation first. Retrying can create a duplicate message.
